items.explanation: ガ is 'ga': カ ('ka') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana が. The two small ticks ゛ are called dakuten. They make the consonant voiced, meaning your vocal cords buzz: k becomes g, s becomes z, t becomes d, and h becomes b. Touch your throat while saying 'k' and then 'g' to feel the difference. In the middle of words some speakers, especially older ones, soften it to a nasal 'nga'; both are correct.
items.mnemonic: カ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'ka' starts to buzz and becomes 'ga'.

items.explanation: ギ is 'gi': キ ('ki') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ぎ. Always a hard g, as in 'give', never as in 'giant'.
items.mnemonic: キ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'ki' starts to buzz and becomes 'gi'.

items.explanation: グ is 'gu': ク ('ku') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ぐ.
items.mnemonic: ク plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'ku' starts to buzz and becomes 'gu'.

items.explanation: ゲ is 'ge': ケ ('ke') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana げ. Always a hard g, as in 'get'.
items.mnemonic: ケ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'ke' starts to buzz and becomes 'ge'.

items.explanation: ゴ is 'go': コ ('ko') with dakuten. It is the same sound as hiragana ご.
items.mnemonic: コ plus two ticks for buzzing vocal cords: 'ko' starts to buzz and becomes 'go'.
